issues.legal_issue: A gift of an undivided share in divisible property is valid without partition or separate delivery when it falls within the exception for freehold property in a large commercial town.
material_facts: The donor executed a genuine registered deed gifting an undivided share of the property to his son.
The property was divisible and situated in a large commercial town; the deed and plaint described it as commercial property.
The lower courts invalidated the gift because the share was undivided and they found no applicable exception.
issues.conclusion: The gift was not invalid as hiba-bil-musha because it fell within the exception for a share in freehold property in a large commercial town.
issues.legal_principle: Under Muslim law, as stated in Mulla, Principles of Mohammedan Law, 20th edition, paragraph 160, a gift of an undivided share in divisible property is ordinarily irregular but may be perfected by partition and delivery. The stated exceptions include a gift of a share in freehold property in a large commercial town, which is valid from the moment of the gift even if the share is not divided or delivered. The judgment also refers to Section 206 as quoted by the trial court; it cites no earlier cases.

rule.if: gift_validity_suit and genuine_gift_deed and divisible_undivided_share and freehold_commercial_property_in_large_town

predicates.gift_validity_suit: A court proceeding concerns whether a gift of property is valid.
predicates.genuine_gift_deed: The donor genuinely executed a deed gifting the share.
predicates.divisible_undivided_share: The deed gifted an undivided share in property capable of division.
predicates.freehold_commercial_property_in_large_to: The gifted share was in freehold commercial property situated in a large commercial town.

issues.definition: When a validity proceeding concerns a genuine gift of an undivided share in divisible property that is freehold commercial property in a large town, the gift is valid without partition or delivery.

issues.legal_issue: A gift of tenanted immovable property satisfies the possession requirement when the deed transfers the right to collect rent from the tenants.
material_facts: The property was occupied by tenants.
The donor executed a genuine registered deed gifting a share to the donee and transferring to him the right to collect the corresponding rent.
The lower courts found that actual or symbolic possession had not been delivered.
issues.conclusion: The possession requirement was met because the property was tenanted and the deed transferred the right to collect rent to the donee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Muslim law, as stated in Mulla, Principles of Mohammedan Law, 20th edition, paragraph 152(2), a gift of immovable property occupied by tenants may be completed by a request that the tenants attorn to the donee, delivery of the title deed, or mutation in the relevant register. The court held on these facts that transferring the right to collect rent under the genuine gift deed met the possession requirement. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: gift_validity_suit and genuine_gift_deed and property_occupied_by_tenants and rent_collection_right_transferred

predicates.gift_validity_suit: A court proceeding concerns whether a gift of property is valid.
predicates.genuine_gift_deed: The donor genuinely executed a deed gifting the property or a share in it.
predicates.property_occupied_by_tenants: Tenants occupied the gifted property when the gift was made.
predicates.rent_collection_right_transferred: The deed transferred to the donee the right to collect rent from the tenants.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about a gift, when a genuine deed transfers a share in tenant-occupied property and the right to collect its rent, the possession requirement is satisfied.
